channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Central Asia's Trade and Investment with Gulf States See Significant Growth
item.description: Trade between Central Asia and Gulf states has nearly quadrupled between 2020 and 2025, reaching $3.9 billion. Gulf investment in the region also tripled, exceeding $31.1 billion by mid-2026, with power generation being a key sector. High transportation costs are expected to slow future trade expansion.

item.title: Former Afghan Security Officer Killed by Unidentified Gunmen in Pakistan's Balochistan
item.description: Sharifullah, a former local police commander from Afghanistan's Ghazni Province, was killed by unidentified gunmen in the Sarwanan market in Pakistan's Balochistan province. He had fled to Iran after the Taliban takeover and later moved to Pakistan after an attack there. No group has claimed responsibility.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Leaders Award Each Other Medals
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev began a two-day state visit to Oman. He was met by Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said. High-level talks were held at the 'Al-Alam' palace, focusing on bilateral cooperation and regional/international issues. Business delegation meetings also took place.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Allows Officials to Earn Additional Income
item.description: Officials in Kyrgyzstan are now permitted to engage in additional paid work in education, science, and other professional fields, provided they obtain management approval. This work must not interfere with their primary official duties. The new regulation aims to allow for supplementary earnings.

item.title: 120 Afghan Women Urge French President to Expedite Asylum Applications
item.description: One hundred twenty Afghan women in Iran and Pakistan have appealed to French President Emmanuel Macron to increase humanitarian visa quotas and speed up asylum processing. They fear deportation to Afghanistan due to past activities. The group includes activists, journalists, and former military officers.

item.title: South Korea Donates $6 Million for Afghan Returnees and Affected Communities
item.description: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has launched a $6 million project funded by South Korea to support returnees, displaced persons, and victims of natural disasters in five Afghan provinces. The 'REVIVE Plus' project focuses on infrastructure reconstruction, livelihood recovery, and improving basic services, aiming to benefit over 386,000 people directly and indirectly.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Awarded Oman's Highest State Decoration
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has been honored with Oman's highest state award, the 'Al-Said' Order. In a reciprocal gesture, the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, was presented with the Uzbek 'Order of Friendship' of the highest degree. This exchange highlights the strong diplomatic ties between the two nations.

item.title: FAO Provides Financial Support to Agricultural Businesses in Nine Afghan Provinces
item.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) is offering cash assistance to agricultural businesses and related industries in nine Afghan provinces. Funded by the Asian Development Bank, the initiative aims to strengthen food security and health services, with grants ranging from $5,000 to $15,000.

item.title: Man Arrested in Qashqadaryo for Promising to Sell 36 Hectares of Land
item.description: A man has been arrested in Qashqadaryo for allegedly promising to sell 36 hectares of land for $18,500. The individual reportedly agreed to transfer the land, leased for 49 years, to another person through his contacts in the local administration.

item.title: US, Russia, Israel Oppose Restrictions on Autonomous Weapons Systems
item.description: The United States, Russia, and Israel are against imposing mandatory international restrictions on autonomous weapons capable of independently selecting and engaging targets. Discussions on regulating such systems are ongoing at a UN conference in Geneva, with most nations favoring a treaty.

item.title: Uzbekistan Declares 2026-2036 National Renaissance Period
item.description: During a ceremony marking the 35th anniversary of independence, Uzbekistan's President declared 2026-2036 as a period of national renaissance. Seven priority national programs will be implemented, focusing on education, healthcare, water resources, law, and foreign policy. Regional officials highlighted efforts to study heritage and develop historical sites.

item.title: Afghanistan: UN Reports 9.9 Million Received Humanitarian Aid
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) announced that 9.9 million people in Afghanistan received humanitarian assistance between January and September. Food and agricultural support reached 5.1 million, healthcare served 4.5 million, and essential aid went to 3.5 million. Funding remains significantly short of the required budget.

item.title: Journalists Lose Jobs in Kandahar After Cricket Broadcast Ban
item.description: Several journalists and sports presenters have lost their jobs in Kandahar following the Taliban's ban on broadcasting cricket news and live matches. Media outlets have been forced to stop cricket-related programs. This ban exacerbates existing media restrictions and job losses for journalists in Afghanistan, with many female journalists unable to continue working.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Imposes Six-Month Ban on White Sugar Imports
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has temporarily banned the import of white sugar for six months. The decision aims to stabilize market prices, ensure food security, and develop the domestic sugar market, according to the Cabinet of Ministers.

item.title: Three-Year Moratorium Imposed on Fishing in Issyk-Kul and Song-Kul Lakes
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's cabinet has adopted a resolution to implement a three-year moratorium on commercial fishing in Issyk-Kul and Song-Kul lakes. This measure aims to preserve and increase fish stocks. The Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry will oversee artificial breeding and management efforts.

item.title: Kazakhstan Changes Mobile Number Portability Rules, Reducing Verification Time
item.description: Starting November 24, Kazakhstan is altering its mobile number portability procedures. The verification time for subscribers wishing to switch operators while keeping their number will be reduced from 35 minutes to 10 minutes. However, the overall porting period remains unchanged for individuals and legal entities.

item.title: German Court Upholds Deportation of Afghan National for Online Extremist Content
item.description: A German court in North Rhine-Westphalia has confirmed the deportation of an Afghan citizen for publishing extremist content on social media. The individual had allegedly promoted 'jihad' and called for the murder of Jews, violating Germany's democratic principles. The court rejected the Afghan's request to halt the immediate deportation.

item.title: Taliban Restrict Afghan Women's Access to Medical Care
item.description: In most Afghan provinces, male doctors are now prohibited from examining or treating women unless a male guardian is present. These restrictions apply even in emergencies. Taliban representatives reportedly inspect clinics, threatening doctors with imprisonment for non-compliance. A shortage of female medical staff exacerbates the situation, as women are banned from medical education and employment.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Leaders Hold Meeting, Discuss Relations
item.description: Leaders of Uzbekistan and Oman held a meeting, noting the active development of relations between the two countries in recent years. Political dialogue has been strengthening, and trade-economic and cultural-humanitarian ties are consistently expanding. The meeting focused on enhancing bilateral cooperation.

item.title: US, China, Russia Leaders to Hold Historic First Trilateral Meeting
item.description: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to hold their first-ever trilateral meeting on November 19th on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China. The primary agenda item will be nuclear non-proliferation.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Discusses New Investment Projects with Omani Business Leaders
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with prominent Omani business representatives in Oman to discuss launching new investment projects. Key areas of focus included increasing the capital of the Uzbek-Omani Investment Company and exploring joint ventures in mining, electrical engineering, chemicals, green energy, urban development, transport, and agriculture. A joint business council was established to foster dialogue and monitor progress.

item.title: Putin, Trump, and Xi Jinping to Meet at APEC Summit in Shenzhen
item.description: Russian, US, and Chinese leaders Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump, and Xi Jinping are finalizing the agenda for a trilateral meeting at the upcoming APEC summit in Shenzhen, China. A joint statement is also being prepared. This meeting is expected to address nuclear non-proliferation and arms reduction, with Trump planning to raise the issue of reducing global nuclear arsenals.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Increase Bank Funding for Mortgages
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to boost bank and mortgage company funding for housing loans from 43% to 60% within three years. President Mirziyoyev stated this would reduce budget burden and save at least 12 trillion UZS. New financing mechanisms are to be proposed to further increase mortgage credit volume by 2027.

item.title: Heating Restored to Bishkek's 10th Microdistrict After Technical Issues
item.description: Heating and hot water supply has been restored to Bishkek's 10th microdistrict after temporary disruptions. The issues were caused by an automatic circuit breaker at a transformer substation failing to withstand electrical load. The faulty breaker has been replaced, and the heating system is now operating normally.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Proposes Announcing Utility Tariffs Years in Advance
item.description: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan proposes announcing future utility tariff changes several years ahead. This would allow households and businesses to plan expenses better. The regulator noted that tariff increases are adding pressure to inflation. The proposal aims to improve predictability in utility costs.

item.title: Jordan and Iraq Ban Telegram Messenger Over Security Concerns
item.description: Jordan and Iraq have announced the blocking of the Telegram messenger due to security concerns and insufficient measures against inappropriate and criminal content. Jordan's Public Security Directorate cited efforts to combat extremism, while Iraq's media organization aims to compel Telegram to review content related to the country and prevent violations. Telegram has been given 30 days to comply with Iraqi laws.

item.title: Afghanistan's Polio-Free Initiative Stresses Vaccination for All Children, Including Sick and Newborns
item.description: Afghanistan's Polio-Free Initiative emphasizes the critical importance of polio vaccination for all children, including newborns and those who are ill. The initiative highlighted that these children, with their weakened immune systems, require enhanced protection against diseases like polio. This message aims to underscore the necessity of vaccinating every child to prevent the disease's continued spread.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman aim to expand trade, economic, and humanitarian ties
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Sultan Haitham bin Tarik of Oman held talks in Muscat, discussing prospects for deepening bilateral partnership. Both leaders noted the steady growth in relations, particularly in political dialogue, trade, economic, and cultural-humanitarian spheres.

item.title: US and Russia Oppose Talks to Limit AI-Controlled Weapons Ahead of UN Discussion
item.description: The US and Russia are reportedly against negotiations to restrict weapons controlled by artificial intelligence. Ahead of a UN discussion on limiting the use of AI-powered weapons, most nations support new international rules, but the US, Russia, and Israel may object.

item.title: Kazakhstan Participates in ICAO Conference Discussing Aviation Future Until 2050
item.description: Kazakhstan is represented at the ICAO World Conference in Montreal, discussing the future of air travel until 2050. The conference, the first in 13 years, addresses new routes, digitalization, airport investments, flight safety, and passenger rights. Kazakhstan aims to discuss civil aviation development with partners.

item.title: Karakalpakstan Reviews Winter Season Preparations
item.description: Karakalpakstan's deputy speaker reviewed winter season preparations in the Karaouzyak district. The review included heating systems, electricity, and gas supply for residents, as well as school heating. Tasks were set to ensure a smooth season, with officials instructed to address identified shortcomings and citizen concerns.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Hold Nationwide Election Infrastructure Test on November 18
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will conduct a nationwide test of its election infrastructure on November 18. Citizens will be able to check their data in voter lists, undergo biometric identification, and familiarize themselves with the voting procedure. This event is part of preparations for upcoming presidential elections.

item.title: Iran's Foreign Minister Meets with Pakistan's Army Chief in Islamabad
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, met with Pakistan's Army Chief, Asim Munir, in Islamabad. The meeting, held on Monday evening, focused on regional and international developments, bilateral relations, and strengthening cooperation to maintain peace and stability in the region.

item.title: Pakistan and Iran Discuss Afghanistan Developments and Regional Issues
item.description: Pakistan's special representative for Afghanistan, Mohammad Sadeq, met with Iran's counterpart, Mohammad Reza Bahrami, in Islamabad. They discussed the latest developments in Afghanistan, regional issues, and exchanged views on matters of mutual interest. Both sides stressed the importance of continued dialogue.

item.title: UNICEF Reports Half of Afghan Children Face Severe Food Poverty
item.description: UNICEF states that half of Afghanistan's children suffer from severe food poverty and lack access to nutritious diets. While treating malnutrition saves lives, prevention is crucial. Around 3.7 million children experienced acute malnutrition in 2026, with 80% of those suffering from wasting being under two years old.

item.title: Ebola Death Toll Rises in the Democratic Republic of Congo
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo has recorded over 11,300 confirmed Ebola cases since May 2026, with 5,568 resulting in death, according to the National Institute of Public Health. The fatality rate stands at 48.9%, with the Ituri province most affected. No certified vaccines exist for this variant.

item.title: Russia Includes Central Asia in Demands for Ukraine War Settlement, NYT Reports
item.description: Russia has presented the US and European nations with demands for ending the war in Ukraine, which also concern Central Asia, according to a non-paper obtained by The New York Times. Russia seeks NATO to cease military activity in the region and revert to pre-1997 borders.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Head Saguimbaev Resigns Amidst Corruption Probe
item.description: Ermek Saguimbaev has been dismissed as head of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB). The official reason cited is a transition to another job and the need for leadership rotation. However, the president reportedly considered missteps by security forces in a corruption incident. Marat Irmenov has been appointed as the new KNB head.

item.title: Belarusian Center for SCO People's Diplomacy Established in Minsk
item.description: A Belarusian Center for People's Diplomacy of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) has been established in Minsk, coinciding with the organization's 25th anniversary. The center aims to strengthen ties between peoples of SCO member states, with similar centers already operating in several countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Boost Economic Ties, Aiming for $500 Million in Trade
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman are expanding economic cooperation, with a goal to reach $500 million in bilateral trade. The sixth meeting of the Uzbek-Omani Joint Intergovernmental Commission in Muscat discussed reducing trade barriers and potential joint projects valued at $5 billion. This collaboration aims to leverage economic potential and attract Omani investments into Uzbekistan's industries.
